---
title: "Equations and numerical methods"
---

## GLM magnetohydrodynamics {#sec-glm}

The MHD state stores nine conserved fields in structure-of-arrays order
`(rho, rho*vx, rho*vy, rho*vz, E, Bx, By, Bz, psi)`. Code magnetic units absorb
`4*pi`, so magnetic pressure is `B^2/2`, not `B^2/(8*pi)`.
{{< src "lib/MHDKernels/src/state.jl" "allocate_state" >}}

The local ideal-MHD flux operator has continuity, momentum, and induction terms

$$
\partial_t\rho+\nabla\cdot(\rho\mathbf v)=0,
\qquad
\partial_t(\rho\mathbf v)+\nabla\cdot\left[
\rho\mathbf v\mathbf v+(p+B^2/2)\mathbf I-\mathbf B\mathbf B\right]
=\mathbf S_m,
$$ {#eq-mhd-momentum}

$$
\partial_t\mathbf B+\nabla\cdot(\mathbf v\mathbf B-\mathbf B\mathbf v)
+\nabla\psi=0,
\qquad
p=(\gamma-1)\left(E-\frac{\rho v^2}{2}-\frac{B^2}{2}\right).
$$ {#eq-induction}

Here the induction tensor is understood componentwise as the flux
`v_j B_i - B_j v_i` in direction `j`. The GLM scalar propagates magnetic
divergence at the cleaning speed and is damped by the mixed hyperbolic/parabolic
cleaning update. The energy flux is
`(E+p+B^2/2)*v - (v dot B)*B`; external gravity, drag, expansion-aware chemistry,
and radiation response are coupled by their respective source updates, not
inserted as an unqualified isolated-box conservation law.
{{< src "lib/MHDKernels/src/glm_physics.jl" "glm" >}}

The production scheme uses finite-volume Godunov updates with PPM reconstruction
and HLLD [@miyoshi2005] with GLM cleaning [@dedner2002] unless configured
otherwise; PLM is used by the tiny installation
examples. LLF fallback and positivity handling can change the local numerical
diffusion and must be monitored. A portable reference integrator and fused cube
integrator coexist. Shared source is not a substitute for backend parity tests.

## Magnetic-force decomposition {#sec-force-split}

The centered Maxwell-stress diagnostic uses

$$
\mathbf F_P=-\nabla(B^2/2),\qquad
\mathbf F_T=\nabla\cdot(\mathbf B\mathbf B),\qquad
\mathbf F_L=\mathbf F_P+\mathbf F_T.
$$ {#eq-maxwell}

The divergence form equals `(B dot grad) B` only when magnetic divergence is
negligible. The force used by the radiation coupling and diagnostic split uses
the same centered stencil.
{{< src "lib/MHDKernels/src/terminal_ct.jl" "terminal_magnetic_force_split!" >}}

## Expansion, units, and clocks {#sec-clocks}

The run evolves `a=1/(1+z)` and a dimensionless supercomoving clock `tau` with

$$
\frac{da}{d\tau}=
\sqrt{a^3\left(\Omega_m+\Omega_\Lambda a^3+\Omega_k a+\Omega_r/a\right)},
\qquad \Omega_k=1-\Omega_m-\Omega_\Lambda-\Omega_r.
$$ {#eq-clock}

Radiation density is included in early starts. The driver converts this clock
to physical source times and MHD code time; it does **not** equate an MHD step
to a physical second. `legacy` and `jedamzik` clock scalings are distinct
model choices, with the facade using the latter for cosmological runs.
{{< src "src/production/runner.jl" "dadtau" >}}
{{< src "src/production/runner.jl" "function _hydro_time_per_tau" >}}

For a comoving field amplitude in nG specified at `z_ref`, the initializer uses

$$
B_{\rm phys}=10^{-9}B_{0,\rm nG}(1+z_{\rm ref})^2\ {\rm G},\qquad
B_{\rm code}=\frac{B_{\rm phys}}{v_{\rm unit}\sqrt{4\pi\rho_b(z_{\rm ref})}}.
$$ {#eq-field-units}

`3 pG = 0.003 nG`. The physical density follows the selected baryon cosmology.
`MHD_CHEM_VUNIT` is in cm/s; it is not a box velocity in km/s. The pressure
initializer with `pressure="auto"` uses the same CMB convention as the
chemistry, `T_CMB=2.725(1+z) K`, including particle-number contributions from
helium and electrons.
{{< src "src/production/runner.jl" "function _pmf_code_brms_from_comoving_ng" >}}
{{< src "src/production/runner.jl" "function _cosmological_ionized_p0" >}}

The TOML box is ckpc/h. The facade divides it by `h` for the driver's comoving
ckpc length. The diagnostic spectrum has a separate numeric box parameter;
see [wavenumber units](notation.qmd#sec-wavenumbers) before plotting it.

## Photon-baryon response {#sec-photon-model}

The evolved-moment closure retains photon density and three photon velocity
components. In its linear Fourier response subproblem, consistent code-time
derivatives obey

$$
\begin{aligned}
\delta_b'&=-i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf v_b,\\
\mathbf v_b'&=-i\mathbf k c_s^2\delta_b+
\Gamma(\mathbf v_\gamma-\mathbf v_b)+\mathbf F_{\rm MHD},\\
\delta_\gamma'&=-\tfrac43 i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf v_\gamma,\\
\mathbf v_\gamma'&=-\tfrac14 i c^2\mathbf k\delta_\gamma+
R\Gamma(\mathbf v_b-\mathbf v_\gamma)-S_\gamma(k)\mathbf v_\gamma,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-photon-moments}

where `R=3*rho_b*c^2/(4*rho_gamma_energy)` and `Gamma` is the converted
Compton-drag rate. Equal and opposite scattering momentum transfers recover
the tight-coupling sound speed `c^2/[3(1+R)]`. An algebraic nonlocal stress
closure replaces independent quadrupole fields, approaching diffusion damping
at small `k*lambda_gamma` and phase mixing toward free streaming.
{{< src "lib/MHDKernels/src/radiation_coupling.jl" "_photon_stress_rates" >}}

`moments` uses a second-order L-stable SDIRK response; `moments_exponential`
is the exponential variant chosen by the facade. They should not be described
as identical integrators. Legacy `angular` and `bridge` models remain comparison
options, not higher-order photon hierarchies.

The full MHD update remains active. Spectral predictors and correctors adjust
both density and velocity relative to local drag, avoiding double-counting its
effect. Default photon ICs are adiabatic and comoving with gas; controls are
`MHD_RADIATION_PHOTON_ADIABATIC` and `MHD_RADIATION_PHOTON_COMOVING`.
{{< src "lib/MHDKernels/src/radiation_coupling.jl" "step_radiation_godunov!" >}}

The positive `MHD_RADIATION_FREE_STREAM_TOL` optimization can omit the spectral
gas correction when its bound is small, while still evolving photons. Compare
against zero tolerance before interpreting its accuracy or speed.

## Gravity and chemistry {#sec-gravity-chemistry}

The periodic Poisson solve removes the homogeneous source and combines gas and
lattice-DM perturbations with the configured baryon/DM weights. The default
midpoint density source and particle updates are time-centered. Lattice
displacements reduce cancellation when tiny density perturbations are evolved;
they are not an imported cosmological particle realization.
{{< src "lib/MHDKernels/src/gravity_coupling.jl" "gravity" >}}
{{< src "src/production/runner.jl" "_assemble_total_perturbation_k!" >}}

The full mixing chemistry couples hydrogen/helium abundances, thermal energy,
and recombination response. The facade uses symmetric half-steps around MHD and
an expansion-aware source clock. Centered hydrogen storage protects small
perturbations relative to a changing homogeneous ionization reference; it must
be reconstructed before interpreting an abundance array as `x_HII`.
{{< src "src/production/runner.jl" "chem_hydrogen_storage" >}}

Gaussian smoothing approximates mixing. Optional nonlocal response tables add
a separately modeled, support-limited response. Neither path solves full
three-dimensional Lyman-alpha transfer; [validation limits](validation.qmd#sec-limitations)
are part of the model specification.
